494	/**
495	 * Clone the committed tip, make the clean checkout, and install it. The
496	 * sparse patterns are set before the first checkout, and git gives every
497	 * worktree added from the clone the same patterns, so the program's
498	 * department and integration worktrees leave the same directories out.
499	 */
500	function prepare(options: IntakeOptions, run: string, head: string): { repo: string; tip: string } {
501	  const repo = join(run, 'repo')
502	  const tip = join(run, 'tip')
503	  mkdirSync(run, { recursive: true })
504	  git(['clone', '--quiet', '--no-tags', '--no-checkout', options.root, repo], run)
505	  if (options.exclude.length > 0) {
506	    git(['sparse-checkout', 'set', '--no-cone', '/*', ...options.exclude.map(dir => `!/${dir}/`), `/${KEPT_DIRECTORY}/`], repo)
507	    // The sparse patterns live in per-worktree config, so git enables the
508	    // `worktreeConfig` extension, and a repository using an extension is
509	    // format 1; the repository's own hook installer refuses it at format 0.
510	    git(['config', 'core.repositoryFormatVersion', '1'], repo)
511	  }
512	  git(['checkout', '--quiet', '--detach', head], repo)
513	  git(['config', 'user.name', 'Program Departments intake'], repo)
514	  git(['config', 'user.email', 'intake@daliesk.invalid'], repo)
515	  git(['worktree', 'add', '--quiet', '--detach', tip, head], repo)
516	  if (options.install !== 'none') {
517	    log(`installing the clean checkout: ${options.install}`)
518	    const result = spawnSync('bash', ['-c', options.install], { cwd: tip, encoding: 'utf8' })
519	    writeFileSync(join(run, 'install.log'), `${result.stdout}${result.stderr}`)
520	    if (result.status !== 0) throw new Error(`${options.install} exited ${String(result.status)} in ${tip}; see ${join(run, 'install.log')}`)
521	  }
522	  // An install may give the clean checkout the repository's own git hooks.
523	  // The departments commit in worktrees with no dependencies installed, where
524	  // those hooks cannot run, so every other worktree of the clone runs none.
525	  const hooks = join(run, 'hooks')
526	  mkdirSync(hooks, { recursive: true })
527	  git(['config', 'core.hooksPath', hooks], repo)
528	  return { repo, tip }
529	}

531	/** Run the driver over the plan and return its result line. */
532	async function runDriver(options: IntakeOptions, run: string, repo: string): Promise<DriverResult> {
533	  const stdout = createWriteStream(join(run, 'stdout.jsonl'))
534	  const stderr = createWriteStream(join(run, 'stderr.txt'))
535	  const code = await new Promise<number>((resolveExit, reject) => {
536	    const child = spawn(join(REPO_ROOT, 'node_modules/.bin/tsx'), [join(INTAKE_FIXTURE, 'driver.ts'), options.composition], {
537	      cwd: run,
538	      env: {
539	        ...process.env,
540	        TSX_TSCONFIG_PATH: join(REPO_ROOT, 'tsconfig.json'),
541	        DSH_TEST_PROGRAM_REPO: repo,
542	        DSH_TEST_SESSION_ROOT: join(run, '.sessions'),
543	        DSH_INTAKE_PLAN: join(run, 'plan.json'),
544	      },
545	      stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'pipe'],
546	    })
547	    // A signal to the intake ends the driver with it, so no program outlives the command.
548	    const forward = (): void => {
549	      child.kill('SIGTERM')
550	    }
551	    process.once('SIGTERM', forward)
552	    process.once('SIGINT', forward)
553	    child.stdout.pipe(stdout)
554	    child.stderr.pipe(stderr)
555	    child.on('error', reject)
556	    child.on('close', (exitCode) => {
557	      process.off('SIGTERM', forward)
558	      process.off('SIGINT', forward)
559	      resolveExit(exitCode ?? 1)
560	    })
561	  })
562	  await Promise.all([new Promise(done => stdout.end(done)), new Promise(done => stderr.end(done))])
563	  const lines = readFileSync(join(run, 'stdout.jsonl'), 'utf8').trimEnd().split('\n')
564	  const last = lines.at(-1) ?? ''
565	  if (code !== 0 || !last.startsWith('{')) {
566	    const tail = readFileSync(join(run, 'stderr.txt'), 'utf8').slice(-4000)
567	    throw new Error(`the intake driver exited ${code} without a result; stderr tail:\n${tail}`)
568	  }
569	  return JSON.parse(last) as DriverResult
570	}

572	/** The committed proposals of one department: at its certified revision, else at its branch head. */
573	function committedProposals(
574	  repo: string,
575	  programId: string,
576	  seat: string,
577	  revision: string | undefined,
578	  base: string,
579	): { text: string; revision: string } | undefined {
580	  const branch = `program/${programId}/${seat}`
581	  const head = revision ?? spawnSync('git', ['rev-parse', '--verify', '--quiet', branch], { cwd: repo, encoding: 'utf8' }).stdout.trim()
582	  if (head === '' || head === base) return undefined
583	  const shown = spawnSync('git', ['show', `${head}:${proposalsPath(seat)}`], { cwd: repo, encoding: 'utf8' })
584	  return shown.status === 0 ? { text: shown.stdout, revision: head } : undefined

587	/** Copy every session log the run wrote into the record, masked. */
588	function copySessions(sessionsRoot: string, target: string, hits: Record<string, number>): string[] {
589	  const copied: string[] = []
590	  if (!existsSync(sessionsRoot)) return copied
591	  for (const entry of readdirSync(sessionsRoot, { recursive: true, withFileTypes: true })) {
592	    if (!entry.isFile() || entry.name !== 'session.jsonl') continue
593	    const id = basename(entry.parentPath)
594	    const masked = maskCredentials(readFileSync(join(entry.parentPath, entry.name), 'utf8'))
595	    addHits(hits, masked.hits)
596	    mkdirSync(target, { recursive: true })
597	    writeFileSync(join(target, `${id}.jsonl`), masked.text)
598	    copied.push(id)
599	  }
600	  return copied.sort()
601	}

622	/**
623	 * Run one intake over `options.root`.
624	 * @param options - the intake's options.
625	 * @returns the process exit code.
626	 */
627	export async function runIntake(options: IntakeOptions): Promise<number> {
628	  const started = new Date()
629	  const id = intakeId(started)
630	  const at = started.toISOString()
631	  const shift = options.shift ?? id
632	  const record = `${INTAKE_DIR}/${at.slice(0, 10)}-${id}`
633	  const recordDir = join(options.root, record)
634	  const head = git(['rev-parse', 'HEAD'], options.root)
635	  const queue = readQueue(options.root)
636	  const open = openTickets(queue)
637	  if (open.length >= options.minOpen) {
638	    writeJson(join(recordDir, 'result.json'), {
639	      type: 'intake', id, shift, at, target: { commit: head }, outcome: 'nothing-needed', open: open.length, minOpen: options.minOpen,
640	    })
641	    log(`${open.length} open tickets, at least ${options.minOpen}: nothing needed; recorded ${record}/result.json`)
642	    process.stdout.write(`${JSON.stringify({ type: 'intake', id, record, outcome: 'nothing-needed', open: open.length })}\n`)
643	    return 0
644	  }
645	  const roster = readRoster(options.root)
646	  const selected = selectCoordinators(coordinators(roster, options.root, open), options.coordinators, options.count)
647	  if (selected.length === 0) throw new Error('no Program Departments coordinator is selected')
648	  log(`${open.length} open tickets, below ${options.minOpen}: ${selected.map(coordinator => `${coordinator.seat.id} (${coordinator.open.length} open)`).join(', ')}`)
649	  const run = join(options.scratch, `intake-${at.slice(0, 10)}-${id}`)
650	  const { repo, tip } = prepare(options, run, head)
651	  const plan = intakePlan(selected, queue, options, head, tip)
652	  writeFileSync(join(run, 'plan.json'), `${JSON.stringify(plan, null, 2)}\n`)
653	  log(`running the intake program in ${run}`)
654	  const result = await runDriver(options, run, repo)
655	  const limit = result.routeLimit
656	  const runCheck = shellCheckRunner({ tip, commit: head, timeoutMs: options.checkTimeoutMs, outputChars: OUTPUT_CHARS })
657	  const tipRoster = readRoster(tip)
658	  const admitted: Ticket[] = []
659	  const records: CoordinatorRecord[] = []
660	  for (const coordinator of [...selected].sort((left, right) => (left.seat.id < right.seat.id ? -1 : 1))) {
661	    const seat = coordinator.seat.id
662	    const goal = result.report.goals.find(candidate => candidate.key === seat)
663	    const member = result.members.find(candidate => candidate.key === seat)
664	    const status = goal?.status ?? 'pending'
665	    const certified = status === 'certified' || status === 'merged'
666	    const committed = committedProposals(repo, result.report.programId, seat, certified ? goal?.revision : undefined, head)
667	    const admissionStarted = performance.now()
668	    const proposals = committed === undefined ? { value: null } : parseProposals(committed.text)
669	    let admission: Admission = { verdicts: [] }
670	    if ('error' in proposals) {
671	      admission = { verdicts: [], error: proposals.error }
672	    } else if (committed !== undefined) {
673	      admission = await admitProposals(proposals.value, options.maxTickets, { roster: tipRoster, tip, queue, admitted, runCheck })
674	      if (!certified) admission = uncertified(admission)
675	    }
676	    const mine = admission.verdicts.flatMap(verdict => (verdict.ticket === undefined ? [] : [verdict.ticket]))
677	    admitted.push(...mine)
678	    const limited = limit !== undefined && limit.sessionId === member?.sessionId
679	    const ran = member !== undefined && !(result.walled.includes(member.sessionId) && !limited)
680	    const endedAt = member?.endedAt ?? null
681	    records.push({
682	      seat,
683	      subsystem: coordinator.subsystem,
684	      openInSubsystem: coordinator.open.length,
685	      department: {
686	        status,
687	        ...goal?.reason === undefined ? {} : { reason: goal.reason },
688	        ...member === undefined ? {} : { sessionId: member.sessionId },
689	        ...committed === undefined ? {} : { revision: committed.revision },
690	        ...endedAt === null ? {} : { endedAt: new Date(endedAt).toISOString() },
691	        tokens: member?.tokens ?? 0,
692	        seconds: spanSeconds(member?.startedAt ?? null, endedAt) + Math.round((performance.now() - admissionStarted) / 1000),
693	      },
694	      ran,
695	      outcome: functionOutcome(status, mine.map(ticket => ticket.id), limited),
696	      admitted: mine.map(ticket => ticket.id),
697	      proposals: 'error' in proposals ? committed?.text ?? null : proposals.value,
698	      admission,
699	    })
700	    for (const verdict of admission.verdicts) log(`${seat}: ${describeVerdict(verdict)}`)
701	    if (admission.error !== undefined) log(`${seat}: ${admission.error}`)
702	  }
703	  for (const ticket of admitted) writeFileSync(join(options.root, TICKETS_DIR, `${ticket.id}.json`), formatTicket(ticket))
704	  const hits: Record<string, number> = {}
705	  const sessions = copySessions(join(run, '.sessions'), join(recordDir, 'sessions'), hits)
706	  for (const entry of records) addHits(hits, writeJson(join(recordDir, `${entry.seat}.json`), entry))
707	  const outcome = limit === undefined ? 'ran' : 'route-limit'
708	  addHits(hits, writeJson(join(recordDir, 'result.json'), {
709	    type: 'intake',
710	    id,
711	    shift,
712	    at,
713	    target: { commit: head },
714	    outcome,
715	    open: open.length,
716	    minOpen: options.minOpen,
717	    maxTickets: options.maxTickets,
718	    composition: relative(REPO_ROOT, options.composition),
719	    program: {
720	      programId: result.report.programId,
721	      outcome: result.report.outcome ?? null,
722	      mergedRevision: result.report.mergedRevision ?? null,
723	    },
724	    ...limit === undefined ? {} : { routeLimit: routeLimitRecord(limit) },
725	    coordinators: records.map(entry => ({
726	      seat: entry.seat,
727	      subsystem: entry.subsystem,
728	      openInSubsystem: entry.openInSubsystem,
729	      status: entry.department.status,
730	      ran: entry.ran,
731	      outcome: entry.outcome,
732	      tokens: entry.department.tokens,
733	      seconds: entry.department.seconds,
734	      proposals: Array.isArray(entry.proposals) ? entry.proposals.length : 0,
735	      admitted: entry.admitted,
736	      refused: entry.admission.verdicts
737	        .filter((verdict: Verdict) => !verdict.admitted)
738	        .map(verdict => ({ index: verdict.index, code: verdict.code, reason: verdict.reason })),
739	    })),
740	    admitted: admitted.map(ticket => ticket.id),
741	    sessions,
742	    masked: hits,
743	  }))
744	  const ledger = join(options.root, LEDGER_PATH)
745	  mkdirSync(dirname(ledger), { recursive: true })
746	  for (const entry of records.filter(candidate => candidate.ran)) {
747	    appendFileSync(ledger, functionLine({
748	      at: entry.department.endedAt ?? at,
749	      shift,
750	      seat: entry.seat,
751	      division: selected.find(coordinator => coordinator.seat.id === entry.seat)?.seat.division ?? '',
752	      commit: head,
753	      outcome: entry.outcome,
754	      evidence: `${record}/${entry.seat}.json`,
755	      seconds: entry.department.seconds,
756	    }))
757	  }
758	  if (!options.keep) rmSync(run, { recursive: true, force: true })
759	  log(`admitted ${admitted.length === 0 ? 'nothing' : admitted.map(ticket => ticket.id).join(', ')}; recorded ${record}`)
760	  process.stdout.write(`${JSON.stringify({ type: 'intake', id, record, outcome, admitted: admitted.map(ticket => ticket.id), coordinators: records.map(entry => ({ seat: entry.seat, outcome: entry.outcome, ran: entry.ran, admitted: entry.admitted, tokens: entry.department.tokens, seconds: entry.department.seconds })) })}\n`)
761	  if (limit === undefined) return 0
762	  const reset = limit.resetsAt === undefined ? '' : `; its limit lifts at ${new Date(limit.resetsAt).toISOString()}`
763	  process.stderr.write(`enterprise-intake: route ${limit.provider}/${limit.model} stopped at its limit: ${limit.message}${reset}\n`)
764	  return ROUTE_LIMIT_EXIT_CODE
765	}

767	/**
768	 * One department's verifier: admit the proposals it committed, print one line
769	 * per proposal, and pass when at least one is admitted.
770	 * @param options - the `admit` form's options.
771	 * @returns the exit code: 0 when a proposal is admitted, 1 otherwise.
772	 */
773	export async function runAdmit(options: AdmitOptions): Promise<number> {
774	  if (!existsSync(options.proposals)) {
775	    process.stdout.write(`REFUSED: no proposals file is committed at ${options.proposals}\n`)
776	    return 1
777	  }
778	  let proposals: unknown
779	  try {
780	    proposals = JSON.parse(readFileSync(options.proposals, 'utf8')) as unknown
781	  } catch (error: unknown) {
782	    process.stdout.write(`REFUSED: ${options.proposals} is not JSON: ${error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)}\n`)
783	    return 1
784	  }
785	  const commit = git(['rev-parse', 'HEAD'], options.tip)
786	  const admission = await admitProposals(proposals, options.maxTickets, {
787	    roster: readRoster(options.tip),
788	    tip: options.tip,
789	    queue: readQueue(options.root),
790	    admitted: [],
791	    runCheck: shellCheckRunner({ tip: options.tip, commit, timeoutMs: options.checkTimeoutMs, outputChars: 600 }),
792	  })
793	  if (admission.error !== undefined) {
794	    process.stdout.write(`REFUSED: ${admission.error}\n`)
795	    return 1
796	  }
797	  for (const verdict of admission.verdicts) {
798	    process.stdout.write(`${describeVerdict(verdict)}\n`)
799	    const passing = verdict.checks.find(check => check.exitCode === 0)
800	    if (verdict.code === 'passes-before' && passing !== undefined) process.stdout.write(`  ${passing.run} exited 0\n`)
801	  }
802	  const count = admission.verdicts.filter(verdict => verdict.admitted).length
803	  process.stdout.write(`${count} of ${admission.verdicts.length} proposals admitted\n`)
804	  return count > 0 ? 0 : 1
805	}

1	/**
2	 * Admission of the tickets the Program Departments coordinators propose.
3	 *
4	 * A coordinator's department writes its proposals as one JSON array; this
5	 * module decides, deterministically and with no model, which of them enter
6	 * the queue under `data/enterprise/tickets/`. A proposal is admitted only when
7	 * every rule holds, checked in this order:
8	 *
9	 * 1. it is one of the first `maxTickets` entries of the array;
10	 * 2. with the next free id of the queue assigned, {@link validateTickets}
11	 *    accepts it beside every ticket already queued;
12	 * 3. its `seat` is the owner of its `scope`: a seat among the most specific
13	 *    roster seats whose `source` covers every scope entry;
14	 * 4. no open or shipped ticket, and no ticket admitted earlier in the same
15	 *    intake, has the same source path and anchor;
16	 * 5. it carries at least one check of its own, and every one of them fails on
17	 *    a clean checkout of the tip.
18	 *
19	 * A check of its own is every acceptance command except the queue's guards:
20	 * `pnpm run typecheck`, `pnpm run doc-sync`, and the package's coverage run,
21	 * which the queue README states pass before and after a change and which the
22	 * engine runs when it verifies the implemented ticket. A refused proposal takes
23	 * no id, so the admitted ones continue the queue's numbering without a gap.
24	 */

77	/** The status the ledger gives one ticket: closed by a shipped commit, closed by a rejection, or open. */

80	function isRecord(value: unknown): value is Record<string, unknown> {
81	  return typeof value === 'object' && value !== null && !Array.isArray(value)

84	/**
85	 * The status of every ticket the ledger names, from each ticket's latest
86	 * ticket line, by the engine's rule: `shipped` when the line names a shipped
87	 * commit, `rejected` when its review verdict is `reject`, `open` otherwise.
88	 * Function lines and lines that are not JSON objects name no ticket and are
89	 * passed over; the engine owns the ticket line's fields.
90	 * @param text - the ledger file's contents, empty when the file does not exist.
91	 * @returns ticket id to status; a ticket the ledger does not name is open.
92	 */
93	export function ticketStatuses(text: string): Map<string, TicketStatus> {
94	  const statuses = new Map<string, TicketStatus>()
95	  for (const line of text.split('\n')) {
96	    if (line.trim() === '') continue
97	    let parsed: unknown
98	    try {
99	      parsed = JSON.parse(line)
100	    } catch {
101	      // A torn or foreign line names no ticket; the ledger's readers own reporting it.
102	      continue
103	    }
104	    if (!isRecord(parsed) || (parsed['type'] !== undefined && parsed['type'] !== 'ticket')) continue
105	    const ticket = parsed['ticket']
106	    if (typeof ticket !== 'string') continue
107	    const shipped = parsed['shipped']
108	    const review = parsed['review']
109	    if (isRecord(shipped) && typeof shipped['commit'] === 'string') statuses.set(ticket, 'shipped')
110	    else if (isRecord(review) && review['verdict'] === 'reject') statuses.set(ticket, 'rejected')
111	    else statuses.set(ticket, 'open')
112	  }
113	  return statuses
114	}

161	/**

163	 * directory itself, or exactly one file.
164	 * @param source - the seat's repository-relative source.
165	 * @param root - the tree the source is read in.
166	 * @returns the prefix; a directory prefix ends with `/`.
167	 */
168	export function coveredPrefix(source: string, root: string): string {
169	  const trimmed = source.replace(/\/+$/, '')
170	  const slash = trimmed.lastIndexOf('/')
171	  if (trimmed.slice(slash + 1).toLowerCase() === 'readme.md') return slash === -1 ? '' : `${trimmed.slice(0, slash)}/`

173	  return existsSync(absolute) && statSync(absolute).isDirectory() ? `${trimmed}/` : trimmed

176	/**
177	 * Whether a covered prefix contains one repository path.
178	 * @param prefix - a prefix from {@link coveredPrefix}.
179	 * @param path - a scope entry or source path, with or without a trailing `/`.
180	 * @returns true when the path lies at or under the prefix.
181	 */
182	export function covers(prefix: string, path: string): boolean {
183	  if (!prefix.endsWith('/')) return path === prefix
184	  return path.startsWith(prefix) || `${path.replace(/\/+$/, '')}/` === prefix
185	}

187	/**
188	 * The seats that own a scope: among the roster seats whose source covers every
189	 * scope entry, those whose covered prefix is the longest.
190	 * @param roster - the roster.
191	 * @param root - the tree the sources are read in.
192	 * @param scope - the scope entries.
193	 * @returns the owning seat ids, empty when no seat covers every entry.
194	 */
195	export function owningSeats(roster: Roster, root: string, scope: readonly string[]): string[] {
196	  let best = -1
197	  let owners: string[] = []
198	  for (const agent of roster.agents) {
199	    const prefix = coveredPrefix(agent.source, root)
200	    if (scope.length === 0 || !scope.every(entry => covers(prefix, entry))) continue
201	    if (prefix.length > best) {
202	      best = prefix.length
203	      owners = [agent.id]
204	    } else if (prefix.length === best) {
205	      owners.push(agent.id)
206	    }
207	  }
208	  return owners
209	}

242	 * @param all - every coordinator, in roster order.
243	 * @param named - the seat ids `--coordinators` named, or undefined.

248	export function selectCoordinators(all: readonly Coordinator[], named: readonly string[] | undefined, count: number): Coordinator[] {
249	  const ranked = all.map((coordinator, index) => ({ coordinator, index }))
250	    .sort((left, right) => left.coordinator.open.length - right.coordinator.open.length || left.index - right.index)
251	    .map(entry => entry.coordinator)
252	  if (named === undefined) return ranked.slice(0, count)
253	  for (const seat of named) {
254	    if (!all.some(coordinator => coordinator.seat.id === seat)) throw new Error(`--coordinators names ${seat}, which is not a ${INTAKE_DIVISION} coordinator of the roster`)

295	/**

297	 * `data/transcripts/tools/collect-claude-code-session.mjs`, which owns the list
298	 * and does not export it. Keep the two in step.
299	 */
300	const CREDENTIAL_PATTERNS: readonly { readonly name: string; readonly re: RegExp }[] = [
301	  { name: 'anthropic-key', re: /sk-ant-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}/g },
302	  { name: 'openrouter-key', re: /\bsk-or-v1-[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}/g },
303	  { name: 'openai-style-key', re: /\bsk-(?:proj-)?[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}/g },
304	  { name: 'github-token', re: /\b(?:ghp|gho|ghu|ghs|ghr)_[A-Za-z0-9]{30,}|\bgithub_pat_[A-Za-z0-9_]{20,}/g },
305	  { name: 'aws-access-key', re: /\bAKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}\b/g },
306	  { name: 'slack-token', re: /\bxox[abprs]-[A-Za-z0-9-]{10,}/g },
307	  { name: 'private-key', re: /-----BEGIN [A-Z ]*PRIVATE KEY-----/g },
308	  { name: 'bearer-token', re: /\bBearer [A-Za-z0-9._~+/=-]{20,}/g },
309	]

311	/**
312	 * Mask every credential-shaped string. The mask carries only the pattern's
313	 * name and no quote or backslash, so masking a JSON document keeps it JSON.
314	 * @param text - the text to scan.
315	 * @returns the masked text and the number of strings masked per pattern.
316	 */
317	export function maskCredentials(text: string): { text: string; hits: Record<string, number> } {
318	  const hits: Record<string, number> = {}
319	  let masked = text
320	  for (const { name, re } of CREDENTIAL_PATTERNS) {
321	    masked = masked.replace(re, () => {
322	      hits[name] = (hits[name] ?? 0) + 1
323	      return `[masked:${name}]`
324	    })
325	  }
326	  return { text: masked, hits }
327	}

329	/** Environment variable names a spawned acceptance command never receives. */
330	const SECRET_NAME = /KEY|SECRET|TOKEN|PASSWORD/i

332	/**
333	 * The environment an acceptance command runs with: this process's, without any
334	 * variable whose name marks a credential, so a check can neither read one nor
335	 * print one into the evidence, and without the whole `GIT_CONFIG_*` family: git
336	 * refuses every invocation when a `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT` names a key the
337	 * environment no longer carries, and the host configures its credential
338	 * helpers there, which no check of a local checkout needs.
339	 * @param env - the environment to scrub.
340	 * @returns the scrubbed copy.
341	 */
342	export function scrubbedEnvironment(env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv): NodeJS.ProcessEnv {
343	  return Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(env).filter(([name]) => !SECRET_NAME.test(name) && !name.startsWith('GIT_CONFIG_')))
344	}

346	/** Options of {@link shellCheckRunner}. */
347	export interface ShellCheckOptions {
348	  /** The clean checkout every command runs in. */
349	  readonly tip: string
350	  /** The commit the tip is reset to after a command changed it. */
351	  readonly commit: string
352	  /** Wall-clock bound of one command; a command still running then is killed and counts as neither passing nor failing. */
353	  readonly timeoutMs: number
354	  /** Characters of combined output kept as evidence, from the end. */
355	  readonly outputChars: number
356	}

358	/**
359	 * Run acceptance commands with `bash -c` in the tip, one at a time, each in its
360	 * own process group so the timeout ends every process it started. A command
361	 * that leaves the tip changed is recorded and the tip is reset to `commit`
362	 * before the next one, keeping ignored files such as installed dependencies.
363	 * @param options - where and how long each command runs.
364	 * @returns the runner.
365	 */
366	export function shellCheckRunner(options: ShellCheckOptions): RunCheck {
367	  const git = (args: readonly string[]): string => spawnSync('git', args, { cwd: options.tip, encoding: 'utf8' }).stdout
368	  return async (check) => {
369	    const started = performance.now()
370	    const settled = await new Promise<SettledCommand>((resolveRun, reject) => {
371	      const child = spawn('bash', ['-c', check.run], {
372	        cwd: options.tip,
373	        env: scrubbedEnvironment(process.env),
374	        stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'pipe'],
375	        detached: true,
376	      })
377	      let output = ''
378	      const append = (chunk: Buffer): void => {
379	        output = (output + chunk.toString('utf8')).slice(-options.outputChars * 2)
380	      }
381	      child.stdout.on('data', append)
382	      child.stderr.on('data', append)
383	      let timedOut = false
384	      const timer = setTimeout(() => {
385	        timedOut = true
386	        if (child.pid === undefined) return
387	        try {
388	          process.kill(-child.pid, 'SIGKILL')
389	        } catch {
390	          // The group already exited between the deadline and the kill; close still follows.
391	        }
392	      }, options.timeoutMs)
393	      child.on('error', (error) => {
394	        clearTimeout(timer)
395	        reject(error)
396	      })
397	      child.on('close', (exitCode, signal) => {
398	        clearTimeout(timer)
399	        resolveRun({ exitCode, signal, timedOut, output })
400	      })
401	    })
402	    const status = git(['status', '--porcelain']).split('\n').filter(line => line !== '')
403	    const head = git(['rev-parse', 'HEAD']).trim()
404	    if (status.length > 0 || head !== options.commit) {
405	      git(['reset', '--quiet', '--hard', options.commit])
406	      git(['clean', '-fdq'])
407	    }
408	    return {
409	      id: check.id,
410	      run: check.run,
411	      exitCode: settled.exitCode,
412	      signal: settled.signal,
413	      timedOut: settled.timedOut,
414	      seconds: Math.round((performance.now() - started) / 100) / 10,
415	      output: maskCredentials(settled.output.slice(-options.outputChars)).text,
416	      dirtied: head === options.commit ? status : [...status, `HEAD moved to ${head}`],
417	    }
418	  }
419	}

489	/** A candidate with its id replaced and its fields in the queue's order; unknown fields are kept so the validator names them. */
490	function withId(candidate: Record<string, unknown>, id: string): Record<string, unknown> {
491	  const fields: Record<string, unknown> = { ...candidate, id }
492	  const known: readonly string[] = TICKET_FIELDS
493	  const order = [...known.filter(key => key in fields), ...Object.keys(fields).filter(key => !known.includes(key))]

515	/**
516	 * Decide every proposal of one coordinator's file, in file order.
517	 * @param proposals - the parsed file.
518	 * @param maxTickets - how many proposals one coordinator may file; later ones are refused unread.
519	 * @param context - the roster, the tip, the queue, earlier admissions and the check runner.
520	 * @returns one verdict per proposal, or the reason the file cannot be read.
521	 */
522	export async function admitProposals(proposals: unknown, maxTickets: number, context: AdmissionContext): Promise<Admission> {
523	  if (!Array.isArray(proposals)) return { verdicts: [], error: 'the proposals file must hold one JSON array of tickets' }
524	  const batch: Ticket[] = []
525	  const verdicts: Verdict[] = []
526	  for (const [index, entry] of (proposals as unknown[]).entries()) {
527	    const proposal = isRecord(entry) ? entry : undefined
528	    if (index >= maxTickets) {
529	      verdicts.push(refuse(index, proposal, 'over-limit', `only the first ${maxTickets} proposals of a coordinator are admitted`))
530	      continue
531	    }
532	    if (proposal === undefined) {
533	      verdicts.push(refuse(index, proposal, 'invalid', 'a proposal must be a JSON object'))
534	      continue
535	    }
536	    const verdict = await admitOne(index, proposal, batch, context)
537	    verdicts.push(verdict)
538	    if (verdict.ticket !== undefined) batch.push(verdict.ticket)
539	  }
540	  return { verdicts }
541	}

543	async function admitOne(
544	  index: number,
545	  proposal: Record<string, unknown>,
546	  batch: readonly Ticket[],
547	  context: AdmissionContext,
548	): Promise<Verdict> {
549	  const earlier = [...context.admitted, ...batch]
550	  const id = ticketId(context.queue.tickets.length + earlier.length + 1)
551	  const candidate = withId(proposal, id)
552	  const file = `${TICKETS_DIR}/${id}.json`
553	  const loaded: LoadedTicket[] = [
554	    ...context.queue.loaded,
555	    ...earlier.map(ticket => ({ file: `${TICKETS_DIR}/${ticket.id}.json`, value: ticket })),
556	    { file, value: candidate },
557	  ]
558	  const errors = validateTickets(loaded, context.roster, context.tip)
559	    .filter(error => error.startsWith(`${file}: `) || error.includes('numbered without gaps'))
560	    .map(error => error.startsWith(`${file}: `) ? error.slice(file.length + 2) : error)
561	  if (errors.length > 0) return refuse(index, proposal, 'invalid', errors.join('; '))
562	  const ticket = candidate as unknown as Ticket
563	  const owners = owningSeats(context.roster, context.tip, ticket.scope)
564	  if (!owners.includes(ticket.seat)) {
565	    const named = owners.length === 0 ? 'no roster seat covers every scope entry' : `its scope is owned by ${owners.join(' or ')}`
566	    return refuse(index, proposal, 'owner', `seat ${ticket.seat} does not own the scope: ${named}`)
567	  }
568	  const duplicate = [
569	    ...context.queue.tickets.filter(queued => statusOf(context.queue, queued.id) !== 'rejected'),
570	    ...earlier,
571	  ].find(other => other.source.path === ticket.source.path && other.source.anchor === ticket.source.anchor)
572	  if (duplicate !== undefined) {
573	    return refuse(index, proposal, 'duplicate', `${duplicate.id} already carries the source ${ticket.source.path} and its anchor`)
574	  }
575	  const own = ticket.acceptance.filter(check => checkRole(check.run) === 'own')
576	  if (own.length === 0) return refuse(index, proposal, 'no-own-check', 'every acceptance command is a guard that passes before the change; a ticket needs a check of its own that fails before it')
577	  const checks: CheckRun[] = []
578	  for (const check of own) checks.push(await context.runCheck(check))
579	  const timedOut = checks.find(run => run.timedOut)
580	  if (timedOut !== undefined) return refuse(index, proposal, 'timeout', `check ${timedOut.id} did not finish on the clean tip; acceptance must be fast`, checks)
581	  const passing = checks.find(run => run.exitCode === 0)
582	  if (passing !== undefined) return refuse(index, proposal, 'passes-before', `check ${passing.id} already passes on the clean tip, so it certifies nothing`, checks)
583	  return { index, proposedId: typeof proposal['id'] === 'string' ? proposal['id'] : null, title: ticket.title, admitted: true, id, checks, ticket }
584	}

618	  const lines = [

625	    field('task', ticket.task),

627	    `  "acceptance": [\n${ticket.acceptance.map(check => `    { "id": ${JSON.stringify(check.id)}, "run": ${JSON.stringify(check.run)} }`).join(',\n')}\n  ]`,

6	 * its anchor text, and it names a non-empty scope and acceptance.
7	 * `scripts/enterprise-tickets.spec.ts` runs the check over the committed queue.
8	 */

10	import { existsSync, readdirSync, readFileSync, statSync } from 'node:fs'
11	import { basename, isAbsolute, resolve } from 'node:path'
12	
13	import type { Roster } from './enterprise-roster.ts'
14	
15	/** Queue directory, relative to the repository root. */
16	export const TICKETS_DIR = 'data/enterprise/tickets'
17	
18	const TICKET_KEYS = ['id', 'title', 'division', 'seat', 'kind', 'source', 'task', 'scope', 'acceptance', 'budget', 'priority']
19	const SOURCE_KEYS = ['path', 'anchor']
20	const CHECK_KEYS = ['id', 'run']
21	const BUDGET_KEYS = ['maxTotalTokens', 'maxWallMs']
22	const KINDS = new Set(['fix', 'test', 'docs', 'feature', 'chore'])
23	const ID_PATTERN = /^T-\d{4}$/
24	const CHECK_ID_PATTERN = /^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$/
25	/** The task text cites its evidence at least once as `path:line`. */
26	const EVIDENCE_PATTERN = /[\w./-]+\.(?:ts|tsx|md|json|ya?ml|mjs):\d+/
27	const LOWEST_PRIORITY = 3
28	
29	/**
30	 * The acceptance commands one queue requires of every ticket, beside the
31	 * ticket's own. The schema, the seat, the source, the scope, and the check
32	 * format hold for every repository the shift engine runs over; which commands
33	 * a queue mandates is that queue's policy.
34	 */
35	export interface QueuePolicy {
36	  /** Command lines every ticket's acceptance must include verbatim. */
37	  readonly requiredRuns: readonly string[]
38	  /** Fragments at least one acceptance command must contain, each with the rule it stands for. */
39	  readonly requiredFragments: readonly { readonly fragment: string; readonly rule: string }[]
40	  /**
41	   * Command line the shift engine runs at the worktree root over every change
42	   * that touches a Markdown document, whatever the ticket's own acceptance
43	   * says; absent for a queue whose repository has no documentation gate.
44	   */
45	  readonly documentationRun?: string
46	}
47	
48	/**
49	 * This repository's queue: every ticket runs the typecheck and the package's
50	 * per-file coverage, and a change to any Markdown document passes the
51	 * bilingual pairing gate, which a department editing a README pair without
52	 * re-recording it would otherwise ship past the ticket's acceptance.
53	 */
54	export const HARNESS_QUEUE_POLICY: QueuePolicy = {
55	  requiredRuns: ['pnpm run typecheck'],
56	  requiredFragments: [{ fragment: '--coverage', rule: "the package's per-file coverage run" }],
57	  documentationRun: 'pnpm run verify-translation-pairing',
58	}
59	
60	/** A queue that mandates nothing beyond the ticket's own checks, for a repository without this one's gates. */
61	export const OPEN_QUEUE_POLICY: QueuePolicy = { requiredRuns: [], requiredFragments: [] }
62	
63	/** One queue file as read from disk, before validation. */
64	export interface LoadedTicket {
65	  /** Path relative to the repository root. */
66	  readonly file: string
67	  /** Parsed JSON, or the parse failure when the file is not JSON. */
68	  readonly value: unknown
69	}
70	
71	/**
72	 * Read every `T-*.json` under the queue directory in name order.
73	 * @param root - repository root.
74	 * @returns the parsed files; a file that is not valid JSON carries its Error as `value`.
75	 */
76	export function loadTickets(root: string): LoadedTicket[] {
77	  const dir = resolve(root, TICKETS_DIR)
78	  if (!existsSync(dir)) return []
79	  return readdirSync(dir)
80	    .filter(name => /^T-\d{4}\.json$/.test(name))
81	    .sort()
82	    .map((name) => {
83	      const file = `${TICKETS_DIR}/${name}`
84	      try {
85	        return { file, value: JSON.parse(readFileSync(resolve(root, file), 'utf8')) as unknown }
86	      } catch (error: unknown) {
87	        return { file, value: error instanceof Error ? error : new Error(String(error)) }
88	      }
89	    })
90	}
91	
92	function isRecord(value: unknown): value is Record<string, unknown> {
93	  return typeof value === 'object' && value !== null && !Array.isArray(value)
94	}
95	
96	function isNonEmptyString(value: unknown): value is string {
97	  return typeof value === 'string' && value.trim().length > 0
98	}
99	
100	/** A repository-relative path: not absolute, no parent traversal, no leading `./`. */
101	function isRelativePath(value: string): boolean {
102	  return !isAbsolute(value) && !value.startsWith('./') && !value.split('/').includes('..')
103	}
104	
105	function keyErrors(record: Record<string, unknown>, expected: readonly string[], what: string): string[] {
106	  const errors: string[] = []
107	  for (const key of expected) if (!(key in record)) errors.push(`${what} is missing "${key}"`)
108	  for (const key of Object.keys(record)) if (!expected.includes(key)) errors.push(`${what} carries an unknown field "${key}"`)
109	  return errors
110	}
111	
112	function validateSource(source: unknown, root: string): string[] {
113	  if (!isRecord(source)) return ['source must be an object']
114	  const errors = keyErrors(source, SOURCE_KEYS, 'source')
115	  if (errors.length > 0) return errors
116	  const { path, anchor } = source
117	  if (!isNonEmptyString(path) || !isRelativePath(path)) return ['source.path must be a repository-relative path']
118	  const absolute = resolve(root, path)
119	  if (!existsSync(absolute) || !statSync(absolute).isFile()) return [`source.path "${path}" does not exist in the tree`]
120	  if (!isNonEmptyString(anchor)) return ['source.anchor must be a non-empty string']
121	  if (!readFileSync(absolute, 'utf8').includes(anchor)) return [`source.anchor ${JSON.stringify(anchor)} does not occur in "${path}"`]
122	  return []
123	}
124	
125	function validateScope(scope: unknown, root: string): string[] {
126	  if (!Array.isArray(scope) || scope.length === 0) return ['scope must be a non-empty array']
127	  const errors: string[] = []
128	  const seen = new Set<string>()
129	  for (const entry of scope) {
130	    if (!isNonEmptyString(entry) || !isRelativePath(entry)) {
131	      errors.push(`scope entry ${JSON.stringify(entry)} must be a repository-relative path`)
132	      continue
133	    }
134	    if (seen.has(entry)) errors.push(`scope repeats "${entry}"`)
135	    seen.add(entry)
136	    if (!existsSync(resolve(root, entry))) errors.push(`scope prefix "${entry}" does not exist in the tree`)
137	  }
138	  return errors
139	}
140	
141	function validateAcceptance(acceptance: unknown, policy: QueuePolicy): string[] {
142	  if (!Array.isArray(acceptance) || acceptance.length === 0) return ['acceptance must be a non-empty array']
143	  const errors: string[] = []
144	  const ids = new Set<string>()
145	  const runs: string[] = []
146	  acceptance.forEach((check: unknown, index) => {
147	    if (!isRecord(check)) {
148	      errors.push(`acceptance[${index}] must be an object`)
149	      return
150	    }
151	    errors.push(...keyErrors(check, CHECK_KEYS, `acceptance[${index}]`))
152	    const { id, run } = check
153	    if (typeof id !== 'string' || !CHECK_ID_PATTERN.test(id)) errors.push(`acceptance[${index}].id must be a lower-case slug`)
154	    else if (ids.has(id)) errors.push(`acceptance repeats the check id "${id}"`)
155	    else ids.add(id)
156	    if (!isNonEmptyString(run) || run.includes('\n')) errors.push(`acceptance[${index}].run must be one non-empty command line`)
157	    else runs.push(run)
158	  })
159	  for (const required of policy.requiredRuns) {
160	    if (!runs.includes(required)) errors.push(`acceptance must include "${required}"`)
161	  }
162	  for (const { fragment, rule } of policy.requiredFragments) {
163	    if (!runs.some(run => run.includes(fragment))) errors.push(`acceptance must include ${rule}`)
164	  }
165	  return errors
166	}
167	
168	function validateBudget(budget: unknown): string[] {
169	  if (!isRecord(budget)) return ['budget must be an object']
170	  const errors = keyErrors(budget, BUDGET_KEYS, 'budget')
171	  for (const key of BUDGET_KEYS) {
172	    const value = budget[key]
173	    if (!Number.isSafeInteger(value) || (value as number) <= 0) errors.push(`budget.${key} must be a positive integer`)
174	  }
175	  return errors
176	}
177	
178	function validateTicket(loaded: LoadedTicket, roster: Roster, root: string, policy: QueuePolicy): string[] {
179	  const { file, value } = loaded
180	  if (value instanceof Error) return [`not valid JSON: ${value.message}`]
181	  if (!isRecord(value)) return ['a ticket must be a JSON object']
182	  const errors = keyErrors(value, TICKET_KEYS, 'ticket')
183	  const { id, title, division, seat, kind, source, task, scope, acceptance, budget, priority } = value
184	  if (typeof id !== 'string' || !ID_PATTERN.test(id)) errors.push('id must match T-NNNN')
185	  else if (id !== basename(file, '.json')) errors.push(`id "${id}" does not match the file name`)
186	  if (!isNonEmptyString(title)) errors.push('title must be a non-empty string')
187	  const knownDivision = typeof division === 'string' && roster.divisions.some(entry => entry.id === division)
188	  if (!knownDivision) errors.push(`division ${JSON.stringify(division)} is not in the roster`)
189	  const agent = typeof seat === 'string' ? roster.agents.find(entry => entry.id === seat) : undefined
190	  if (agent === undefined) errors.push(`seat ${JSON.stringify(seat)} is not in the roster`)
191	  else if (agent.division !== division) errors.push(`seat "${agent.id}" belongs to division "${agent.division}", not ${JSON.stringify(division)}`)
192	  if (typeof kind !== 'string' || !KINDS.has(kind)) errors.push(`kind ${JSON.stringify(kind)} is not one of ${[...KINDS].join('|')}`)
193	  errors.push(...validateSource(source, root))
194	  if (!isNonEmptyString(task)) errors.push('task must be a non-empty string')
195	  else if (!EVIDENCE_PATTERN.test(task)) errors.push('task must cite its evidence as path:line at least once')
196	  errors.push(...validateScope(scope, root))
197	  errors.push(...validateAcceptance(acceptance, policy))
198	  errors.push(...validateBudget(budget))
199	  if (!Number.isInteger(priority) || (priority as number) < 1 || (priority as number) > LOWEST_PRIORITY) {
200	    errors.push(`priority must be an integer from 1 to ${LOWEST_PRIORITY}`)
201	  }
202	  return errors
203	}
204	
205	/**
206	 * Validate the loaded queue against the roster and the tree.
207	 * @param loaded - the queue files.
208	 * @param roster - the committed roster, for divisions and seats.
209	 * @param root - repository root, for source and scope existence checks.
210	 * @param policy - the acceptance commands this queue mandates; this repository's by default.
211	 * @returns every violation as `<file>: <message>`; empty when the queue is valid.
212	 */
213	export function validateTickets(
214	  loaded: readonly LoadedTicket[],
215	  roster: Roster,
216	  root: string,
217	  policy: QueuePolicy = HARNESS_QUEUE_POLICY,
218	): string[] {
219	  const errors: string[] = []
220	  const ids: string[] = []
221	  for (const ticket of loaded) {
222	    for (const message of validateTicket(ticket, roster, root, policy)) errors.push(`${ticket.file}: ${message}`)
223	    if (isRecord(ticket.value) && typeof ticket.value['id'] === 'string') ids.push(ticket.value['id'])
224	  }
225	  const sorted = [...ids].sort()
226	  sorted.forEach((id, index) => {
227	    const expected = `T-${String(index + 1).padStart(4, '0')}`
228	    if (id !== expected && !errors.some(error => error.includes('numbered without gaps'))) {
229	      errors.push(`${TICKETS_DIR}: ids must be numbered without gaps from T-0001; found "${id}" where "${expected}" was expected`)
230	    }
231	  })
232	  return errors
233	}

1	# enterprise-intake: the coordinators propose the queue's next tickets
2	
3	English | [中文](README.zh.md)
4	
5	The [program](../../../../../packages/improvement/program/README.md) that `pnpm run enterprise:intake` runs when the [ticket queue](../../../../../data/enterprise/tickets/README.md) runs low: one department per Program Departments coordinator of the [roster](../../../../../data/enterprise/README.md), each reading its own package group and committing up to `--max-tickets` proposed tickets, and each measured by admission, the deterministic rules that decide which proposals enter the queue. [`scripts/enterprise-intake.ts`](../../../../../scripts/enterprise-intake.ts) is the command, [`scripts/enterprise-intake-admission.ts`](../../../../../scripts/enterprise-intake-admission.ts) holds the rules, and the [Agent Note](../../../../../.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-09-28-coordinators-intake.md) records why the intake is built this way.
6	
7	## What one intake does
8	
9	1. It counts the open tickets: every ticket under `data/enterprise/tickets/` whose latest ticket line in `data/enterprise/ledger.jsonl` names neither a shipped commit nor a `reject` verdict; an absent ledger leaves every ticket open. At or above `--min-open` (default 8) it writes `result.json` with `outcome: "nothing-needed"` under its record directory and exits 0.
10	2. It selects the coordinators: the seats `--coordinators` names, or the `--count` (default 2) with the fewest open tickets, a coordinator counting every open ticket it owns or whose scope or source lies in its package group, and roster order breaking ties.
11	3. It clones the committed tip into a scratch directory, adds a second worktree of the same commit as the clean checkout the checks run in, and installs it (`--install`, default `pnpm install --offline --frozen-lockfile`). Both leave out `data/` apart from `data/enterprise/` (`--exclude`), and every worktree the program adds from the clone leaves out the same.
12	4. It runs the program through [`driver.ts`](driver.ts): one department per coordinator on the composition's route, each created with the objective [`coordinatorObjective`](../../../../../scripts/enterprise-intake.ts) writes and the composition's caps as its budget, and each certified by one check: `enterprise-intake.ts admit` over the file it committed at `.intake/<seat>.json`, which passes when admission admits at least one proposal. A department whose every proposal was refused is told why and gets one more round. The integration merges the proposal files and is gated on a clean tree.
13	5. It admits every department's committed proposals once more, in department order, so ids and duplicates are decided across departments, and writes each admitted ticket to the queue. A department that did not certify has none admitted.
14	6. It writes its record and appends one function line per coordinator whose department reached the route.
15	
16	## Admission
17	
18	A proposal is admitted only when every rule holds, in this order; a refused proposal takes no id, so the admitted ones continue the queue without a gap.
19	
20	| Rule | Refusal code |
21	|---|---|
22	| It is one of the coordinator's first `--max-tickets` proposals. | `over-limit` |
23	| With the queue's next id assigned, [`validateTickets`](../../../../../scripts/enterprise-tickets.ts) accepts it beside every queued ticket. | `invalid` |
24	| Its `seat` owns its `scope`: among the roster seats whose `source` covers every scope entry, the ones whose covered prefix is longest. A `README.md` source covers its directory, a directory covers itself, a file covers only itself. | `owner` |
25	| No open or shipped ticket, and no ticket admitted earlier in the same intake, has the same `source.path` and `source.anchor`. | `duplicate` |
26	| It carries a check of its own: an acceptance command other than `pnpm run typecheck`, `pnpm run doc-sync` and a `--coverage` run, which pass before and after a change by the queue's rules. | `no-own-check` |
27	| Each check of its own, run with `bash -c` in the clean checkout, exits non-zero within `--check-timeout-ms` (default 120000). | `passes-before`, `timeout` |
28	
29	A check runs in its own process group with every variable whose name carries `KEY`, `SECRET`, `TOKEN` or `PASSWORD` and the whole `GIT_CONFIG_*` set removed from its environment; a check that changed the clean checkout is recorded and the checkout is reset before the next one. Guard commands are not run at admission: the engine runs every acceptance command when it verifies the implemented ticket.
30	
31	## The usage limit
32	
33	[`route-wall.ts`](route-wall.ts) is composed beside the program. The first turn of any session that ends in the LLM seam's `QUOTA` failure — the classification the Claude Code route gives the product's usage-limit notice — walls the process: every later step is rejected before a request is assembled, and the session's goal is blocked under `route-limit`, which the program records as the department's blocking code. The department the refusal cut spends one more validation of what it committed; every department after it is blocked on its first step without a request reaching the route. The intake then admits what certified departments committed, records the refusal with the reset the notice states, and exits 3.
34	
35	## The record and the ledger
36	
37	Every intake writes `data/enterprise/intake/<UTC date>-<hhmmss>-<suffix>/`:
38	
39	| File | What it holds |
40	|---|---|
41	| `result.json` | The target commit, the open count, the outcome (`nothing-needed`, `ran`, `route-limit`), the program's id and outcome, per coordinator its status, tokens, seconds, admitted ids and refusals, the route limit, and the session ids |
42	| `<seat>.json` | One coordinator's department, the proposals it committed, and every verdict with the checks of its own that ran, their exit codes and their output tails |
43	| `sessions/<session id>.jsonl` | Every session log of the program: the ledger, each department, the integration |
44	
45	Credential-shaped strings are masked in every file before it is written, and `result.json` counts the masks per pattern. Each coordinator whose department reached the route gets one line in `data/enterprise/ledger.jsonl`: `{ "type": "function", "at", "shift", "seat", "division", "function": "intake", "target": { "commit" }, "outcome", "evidence": { "path" }, "seconds" }`, with `outcome` `pass` when a ticket of its was admitted, `error` when its department was cut before it finished (a usage limit, a spent budget), and `fail` otherwise, `at` the moment its department's session ended, `evidence.path` its `<seat>.json`, and `shift` the value of `--shift` or the intake's own id. A coordinator whose department the wall stopped before its first request gets no line.
46	
47	## The two compositions
48	
49	[`cordis.yml`](cordis.yml) is the keyless half: the departments run on the `cli-mock` route [`intake-llm.ts`](intake-llm.ts) registers, which reads a script naming, per coordinator seat, either a proposals file under [`scripted/`](scripted) to commit or the product's usage-limit notice to refuse with. [`overlays/claude-code.cordis.yml`](overlays/claude-code.cordis.yml) is the real one: the scripted route disabled, the operator's Claude Code installation inserted with `sonnet` at medium effort, and each department's caps raised to 4,000,000 tokens over 1,500 s.
50	
51	## Running it keyless
52	
53	```sh
54	pnpm exec vitest run --config vitest.e2e.config.ts examples/headless-agent/tests/enterprise-intake.e2e.ts
55	```
56	
57	The e2e is [`examples/headless-agent/tests/enterprise-intake.e2e.ts`](../../enterprise-intake.e2e.ts). It runs the command over repositories minted from [`seed/`](seed), a two-coordinator roster and a one-ticket queue: once at `--min-open 1`, which needs nothing; once with both coordinators, which admits one ticket of each and refuses a proposal whose check already passes and one that repeats the queued ticket's source; and once with the first coordinator refused under the usage-limit notice, which stops the run with no request from the second.
58	
59	## Running it for real
60	
61	From a checkout whose tip is committed, with the `claude` CLI installed and logged in:
62	
63	```sh
64	pnpm run enterprise:intake -- --count 2 --max-tickets 3 --scratch "$SCRATCH"
65	```
66	
67	It writes the admitted tickets, the record and the ledger lines into the checkout and removes its scratch directory unless `--keep` is given; committing them is the operator's act.
68

1	#!/usr/bin/env node
2	/**
3	 * Driver of the intake program: read the plan `scripts/enterprise-intake.ts`
4	 * wrote, turn it into a program spec with one department per coordinator,
5	 * record the two signatures, run the program over the clone the intake
6	 * prepared, and print one result line: the report, every member session's
7	 * spend and span, and the route limit that stopped the run, if one did.
8	 *
9	 * The same driver serves the keyless composition beside it and the Claude Code
10	 * overlay under `overlays/`; what differs is the route the departments are
11	 * driven on and the caps the composition's budget policy states.
12	 */
13	
14	import { createHash } from 'node:crypto'
15	import { existsSync, readFileSync } from 'node:fs'
16	import { join } from 'node:path'
17	import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url'
18	import { boot, resolveConfigPath } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-app-boot'
19	import type {} from '@deepseek-ai/cordis-plugin-loader'
20	import type {} from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent'
21	import type {} from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-default-model'
22	import { foldBudgetSpend } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-budget-policy'
23	import { QUOTA_EXCEEDED_CODE } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm'
24	import { programIdFor, programSpecDigest, resolveProgramSpec } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-program'
25	import type { ProgramGoalBudget, ProgramReport, ProgramSpec } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-program'
26	import { SessionId } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session'
27	import type { SessionEvent } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session'
28	import type { SessionPersistence } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session-persistence'
29	import type {} from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-signoff'
30	import type { CheckId } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-verification/types'
31	import { ROUTE_LIMIT_BLOCK } from './route-wall.ts'
32	
33	/** The plan `scripts/enterprise-intake.ts` writes; its field set changes only together with that script. */
34	interface IntakePlan {
35	  readonly objective: string
36	  readonly baseRevision: string
37	  readonly departments: readonly {
38	    readonly key: string
39	    readonly objective: string
40	    readonly checks: readonly { readonly id: string; readonly outcome: string; readonly run: string }[]
41	  }[]
42	  readonly gates: readonly string[]
43	}
44	
45	/** One member session as the intake reads it. */
46	interface MemberLine {
47	  readonly sessionId: string
48	  readonly key: string
49	  readonly certified: boolean
50	  /** Billed input plus output tokens the session's log accounts for. */
51	  readonly tokens: number
52	  readonly startedAt: number | null
53	  readonly endedAt: number | null
54	  /** Each validation run's verdict, in log order. */
55	  readonly runs: readonly string[]
56	}
57	
58	/** The first turn a route refused under `QUOTA`, which stopped the run. */
59	interface RouteLimitLine {
60	  readonly sessionId: string
61	  readonly provider: string
62	  readonly model: string
63	  readonly message: string
64	  readonly resetsAt?: number
65	}
66	
67	const configPath = process.argv[2]
68	if (configPath === undefined) throw new Error('intake driver requires a config path')
69	
70	/**
71	 * The clone the intake prepared, which the program delivers into.
72	 * @returns its path.
73	 */
74	function preparedRepository(): string {
75	  const path = process.env['DSH_TEST_PROGRAM_REPO']
76	  if (path === undefined || !existsSync(join(path, '.git'))) {
77	    throw new Error('intake driver requires DSH_TEST_PROGRAM_REPO naming the clone the intake prepared')
78	  }
79	  return path
80	}
81	
82	const repository = preparedRepository()
83	const planPath = process.env['DSH_INTAKE_PLAN']
84	if (planPath === undefined) throw new Error('intake driver requires DSH_INTAKE_PLAN')
85	const planBytes = readFileSync(planPath)
86	const plan = JSON.parse(planBytes.toString('utf8')) as IntakePlan
87	
88	/** The artefact both signatures attest: the plan the program was built from. */
89	const ARTEFACT = createHash('sha256').update(planBytes).digest('hex')
90	
91	// The roster's root has to be absolute, so the presets beside this file are exported by path.
92	process.env['DSH_TEST_PROGRAM_PRESETS'] = fileURLToPath(new URL('presets', import.meta.url))
93	
94	// A host that configures git through `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT` hands every child a
95	// command-line config the shell seam cannot forward whole, and git then refuses
96	// every invocation. The program runs against the intake's own clone, so the
97	// whole set is dropped rather than half inherited.
98	for (const key of Object.keys(process.env)) {
99	  if (key.startsWith('GIT_CONFIG_')) Reflect.deleteProperty(process.env, key)
100	}
101	
102	/**
103	 * The caps every department session runs under: the composition's own session
104	 * caps, read from its budget policy, so the overlay's patch of that row is what
105	 * sets a real run's token cap per department.
106	 * @param ctx - the booted application.
107	 * @returns the goal budget each department's `budget/caps` carries.
108	 */
109	function departmentBudget(ctx: Awaited<ReturnType<typeof boot>>): ProgramGoalBudget {
110	  const budgets = ctx.get('sessionBudgets')
111	  if (budgets === undefined) throw new Error('intake driver requires the session budget policy')
112	  const caps = new Map(budgets.configuredCaps())
113	  const maxTotalTokens = caps.get('maxTotalTokens')
114	  const maxWallMs = caps.get('maxWallMs')
115	  const maxCostEur = caps.get('maxCostEur')
116	  return {
117	    ...maxTotalTokens === undefined ? {} : { maxTotalTokens },
118	    ...maxWallMs === undefined ? {} : { maxWallMs },
119	    ...maxCostEur === undefined ? {} : { maxCostEur },
120	  }
121	}
122	
123	/**
124	 * The intake program: one department per coordinator, each measured by its
125	 * admission check, and an integration gated on the merged tree being clean.
126	 * @param budget - the caps every department runs under.
127	 * @returns the spec, frozen and digested before anything runs.
128	 */
129	function programSpec(budget: ProgramGoalBudget): ProgramSpec {
130	  return {
131	    objective: plan.objective,
132	    baseRevision: plan.baseRevision,
133	    signoff: { artefactSha256: ARTEFACT },
134	    goals: plan.departments.map(department => ({
135	      key: department.key,
136	      objective: department.objective,
137	      preset: 'proposing',
138	      isolation: 'none',
139	      budget,
140	      dependsOn: [],
141	      checks: department.checks.map(check => ({ id: check.id as CheckId, outcome: check.outcome, run: check.run })),
142	    })),
143	    integration: { checks: [], gates: [...plan.gates] },
144	  }
145	}
146	
147	/**
148	 * Record the spec-freeze and release signatures on the program session before
149	 * it opens, as the intake's operator. A session that already carries them is
150	 * left alone, so a resumed run signs nothing twice.
151	 * @param ctx - the booted application.
152	 * @param spec - the spec whose digest names the program session.
153	 */
154	async function sign(ctx: Awaited<ReturnType<typeof boot>>, spec: ProgramSpec): Promise<void> {
155	  const sessionId = SessionId(programIdFor(programSpecDigest(resolveProgramSpec(spec))))
156	  const signoffs = ctx.get('signoffs')
157	  const agents = ctx.get('agents')
158	  if (signoffs === undefined || agents === undefined) throw new Error('intake driver requires the signoffs and agents services')
159	  if ((await ctx.get('sessionPersistence')?.list() ?? []).some(stored => stored.id === sessionId)) return
160	  const model = ctx.get('agentDefaultModel')?.currentSelection()
161	  if (model === undefined) throw new Error('intake driver requires the default-model service')
162	  const handle = await agents.create({
163	    sessionId,
164	    meta: { cwd: repository },
165	    agentOptions: { provider: model.provider, model: model.model },
166	  })
167	  try {
168	    for (const transition of ['spec-freeze', 'release'] as const) {
169	      signoffs.record(handle.agent, {
170	        transition,
171	        principal: { kind: 'human', id: 'enterprise-intake-operator', displayName: 'enterprise intake operator' },
172	        artefactSha256: ARTEFACT,
173	        evidence: [{ kind: 'spec', ref: 'the frozen intake program spec over the intake plan' }],
174	      })
175	    }
176	    await ctx.sessions.flush(handle.agent.session)
177	  } finally {
178	    await handle.dispose()
179	  }
180	}
181	
182	/** The first turn of a session that ended in the seam's `QUOTA` failure. */
183	function quotaTurnEnd(events: readonly SessionEvent[]): SessionEvent<'turn/end'> | undefined {
184	  return events.find((event): event is SessionEvent<'turn/end'> =>
185	    event.type === 'turn/end' && event.data.reason.kind === 'error' && event.data.reason.error.code === QUOTA_EXCEEDED_CODE)
186	}
187	
188	/**
189	 * Every member session of the program, and the route limit that stopped it.
190	 * @param persistence - the backend the composition mounted.
191	 * @param report - the report whose program the members belong to.
192	 * @param route - the route every department was created with.
193	 * @returns the member lines, the sessions the wall refused without a request, and the limit.
194	 */
195	async function readMembers(
196	  persistence: SessionPersistence,
197	  report: ProgramReport,
198	  route: { readonly provider: string; readonly model: string },
199	): Promise<{ members: MemberLine[]; walled: string[]; routeLimit?: RouteLimitLine }> {
200	  const members: MemberLine[] = []
201	  const walled: string[] = []
202	  let routeLimit: RouteLimitLine | undefined
203	  let limitAt = Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY
204	  for (const stored of await persistence.list()) {
205	    const { events } = await persistence.inspect(stored.id)
206	    const member = events.find((event): event is SessionEvent<'program/member'> => event.type === 'program/member')
207	    if (member === undefined || member.data.programId !== report.programId) continue
208	    const refused = quotaTurnEnd(events)
209	    if (refused !== undefined && refused.time < limitAt && refused.data.reason.kind === 'error') {
210	      limitAt = refused.time
211	      const { error } = refused.data.reason
212	      routeLimit = {
213	        sessionId: stored.id,
214	        provider: route.provider,
215	        model: route.model,
216	        message: error.message,
217	        ...error.providerRetryAfterMs === undefined ? {} : { resetsAt: refused.time + error.providerRetryAfterMs },
218	      }
219	    }
220	    const goal = report.goals.find(candidate => candidate.key === member.data.key)
221	    if (refused === undefined && goal?.status === 'blocked' && goal.reason === ROUTE_LIMIT_BLOCK) walled.push(stored.id)
222	    members.push({
223	      sessionId: stored.id,
224	      key: member.data.key,
225	      certified: events.some(event => event.type === 'verification/certificate'),
226	      tokens: foldBudgetSpend(events, {}).totalTokens,
227	      startedAt: events[0]?.time ?? null,
228	      endedAt: events.at(-1)?.time ?? null,
229	      runs: events.flatMap(event => (event.type === 'verification/run' ? [event.data.verdict] : [])),
230	    })
231	  }
232	  return { members, walled, ...routeLimit === undefined ? {} : { routeLimit } }
233	}
234	
235	const ctx = await boot('enterprise-intake', resolveConfigPath(configPath, undefined))
236	try {
237	  // Loader siblings mount concurrently; the program mounts presets and reads
238	  // persisted sessions, so the driver drives only the settled application.
239	  await ctx.get('loader')?.await()
240	  const programs = ctx.get('programs')
241	  const persistence = ctx.get('sessionPersistence')
242	  const route = ctx.get('agentDefaultModel')?.currentSelection()
243	  if (programs === undefined || persistence === undefined || route === undefined) {
244	    throw new Error('intake driver requires the programs, session persistence and default-model services')
245	  }
246	  const spec = programSpec(departmentBudget(ctx))
247	  await sign(ctx, spec)
248	  const report = await programs.start(spec)
249	  const observed = await readMembers(persistence, report, route)
250	  process.stdout.write(`${JSON.stringify({ type: 'result', report, ...observed })}\n`)
251	} finally {
252	  await ctx.fiber.dispose()
253	}

# AGENTS.md — Examples

Runnable harness compositions. `examples/` is one workspace member and the module-resolution root for runnable and test Cordis configs; it is not a build target. [package.json](package.json) declares the packages loaded by those configs, while each leaf's private `package.json` remains metadata only.

Extract reusable logic into `packages/`, where per-file coverage and README gates apply. Examples keep only `cordis.yml` wiring, demo artifacts, and e2e/snapshot scenarios; app package bins own boot glue.

## E2E smokes

Each example has both:

- **Keyless:** boot the real `cordis.yml` through the Loader, drive it, and assert output and clean exit. Catches invalid Loader exports that hand-mounted tests miss ([postmortem](../docs/postmortem/0001-acp-default-export-drops-inject.md)).
- **With-key:** send a live-model prompt and verify external state, not the model's claim. Self-skip without `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`; see [testing.md](../docs/testing.md).

Keyless process smokes use `@deepseek-ai/dsh-loader-smoke` for Loader launch resolution; terminal tests wrap that launch in a pseudo-terminal. Tests supply paths, environment, input, and assertions. Every checked-in test Cordis config lives under its corresponding `examples/<agent>/` leaf. Map a package-owned config to `examples/<agent>/tests/fixtures/<group>/<package>/cordis.yml`, keep its driver and assertions package-local, and declare every package it names in both root `tsconfig.json` references and `examples/package.json`.

Do not inventory example tests here; the `tests/` trees and root scripts are authoritative.

In `cordis.yml`, comment only non-obvious wiring, load-order consequences, replay, security boundaries, and configuration scope. Do not narrate visible entries; use [dsh-prose-standard](../.agents/skills/dsh-prose-standard/SKILL.md) for required coverage and editorial judgment.

See [the root AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md) for repo-wide conventions and [docs/architecture.md](../docs/architecture.md) for the design.

154	    ['merged', [], false, 'fail'],
155	    ['blocked', [], true, 'error'],
156	    ['blocked', [], false, 'error'],
157	    ['failed', [], true, 'error'],
158	    ['abandoned', [], false, 'error'],
159	  ] as const)('reads a %s department that admitted %j (limited: %s) as %s', (status, admitted, limited, outcome) => {
160	    expect(functionOutcome(status, admitted, limited)).toBe(outcome)
161	  })
162	
163	  it('writes one function line with the shared field set, in order', () => {
164	    const line = functionLine({
165	      at: '2026-09-28T17:20:00.000Z',
166	      shift: '172000-abcd',
167	      seat: GOAL,
168	      division: 'program-departments',
169	      commit: 'c'.repeat(40),
170	      outcome: 'pass',
171	      evidence: `data/enterprise/intake/2026-09-28-172000-abcd/${GOAL}.json`,
172	      seconds: 42,
173	    })
174	    expect(line.endsWith('\n')).toBe(true)
175	    expect(JSON.parse(line)).toEqual({
176	      type: 'function',
177	      at: '2026-09-28T17:20:00.000Z',
178	      shift: '172000-abcd',
179	      seat: GOAL,

185	      seconds: 42,
186	    })
187	    expect(Object.keys(JSON.parse(line) as object)).toEqual(['type', 'at', 'shift', 'seat', 'division', 'function', 'target', 'outcome', 'evidence', 'seconds'])
